title: every bash suite runs in exactly one CI shard: the shards share one timings read, and the required ci check fails unless the shards together ran tests/*.test.sh each exactly once
acceptance: Why. On PR #180 head 7efe000 (run 37218411231) fail-first reported tests/board-readiness.test.sh failing its new assertion, yet all six `bash suites` shards were green: the suite ran in no shard. The six shard logs list 158 suite runs over 123 distinct suites of the 159 in tests/*.test.sh; 36 suites ran nowhere (board-readiness, decide, i18n, emit, evidence-binding, config, worker-policy among them) and several ran twice. Cause: each bash shard downloads 'the latest successful main run' timings itself (.github/workflows/ci.yml:63-73, step 'previous suite timings') and bin-packs with `shard_suites` (bin/ci.sh:162-181, used at :424). Main run 37218262512 went green at 16:56:10Z while the shards started between 16:55:40Z and 16:56:17Z, so shards 1, 3 and 6 packed with one timings file (predicted mean 709.2s) and shards 2, 4 and 5 with another (737.4s): two different partitions. Fail-first already fixed this race for itself with one `fail-first-timings` job (ci.yml:146-173, whose comment describes this exact failure); the bash shards never got the fix. A per-shard download that fails (`|| true`, :70-72) gives the same divergence. Any PR and any push to main can silently skip suites, and gate 6 reads that `ci` result.

One timings read for the bash shards. Add a job `bash-timings` (name 'bash timings') to .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs on every event (no `if:`), with `timeout-minutes: 10`, and whose single step reads the timings exactly as today's bash-shard step does (latest successful `ci.yml` run on main, artifacts `suite-timings-*`, best effort, never failing) and exposes them as a job output `timings` using the same heredoc-delimiter form `fail-first-timings` uses (`timings<<FM_TIMINGS_END`, filtering a literal `FM_TIMINGS_END` line). The `bash` matrix job gets `needs: [bash-timings]`, loses its own 'previous suite timings' step, and its 'bin/ci.sh --stage bash --shard' step writes `${{ needs.bash-timings.outputs.timings }}` (passed through an env var, as fail-first-shard passes FM_FF_TIMINGS) to /tmp/timings.txt before running `bash bin/ci.sh --stage bash --shard "${{ matrix.shard }}/6"` with FM_CI_TIMINGS_IN=/tmp/timings.txt. FM_CI_TIMINGS_OUT and the `suite-timings-<shard>` upload stay as they are. `fail-first-timings`, `fail-first-shard` and `fail-first` are unchanged (their pins in tests/failfirst.test.sh:440-460 stay green); consolidating them onto bash-timings is out of scope.

The shard says what it was assigned. bin/ci.sh gains FM_CI_ASSIGNED_OUT=path, documented in the header comment next to FM_CI_TIMINGS_OUT (:17-22). When it is set and `want_stage bash` is true, bin/ci.sh writes the file as soon as `shard_indices` is known and before the pool starts (just before :527), even when the shard has no suites: first line `# shard i/n` for `--shard i/n`, or `# shard 1/1` with no --shard; then one line per assigned suite, the path exactly as in `suites[$i]` (e.g. `tests/emit.test.sh`), in shard_indices order. It is written to the given path, created with its directory, never under FM_ROOT unless the path says so, and never when the variable is unset (the plain run writes nothing new). Writing it before any suite runs means it records the assignment, not the outcome; a suite that is assigned but fails or never finishes still fails the shard as today (:1178-1205).

The coverage check is a mode of bin/ci.sh, so the workflow runs no logic of its own (ci.yml header rule). `bin/ci.sh --coverage <dir>` runs no stage: it is parsed in the option loop with the inline value guard ci.sh uses for --plan (:59-65; this file is exempt from fm_need per tests/option-loop.test.sh), refuses --stage, --shard and --plan alongside it with exit 64, honours FM_ROOT like --plan does (:198-203, including refusing FM_ROOT set but empty), and reads every `*.txt` file directly in <dir>. It exits 0 only if all hold: (1) at least one file exists; (2) every file's first line is `# shard i/n` with the same n in all files and each i in 1..n present exactly once (a missing shard, a duplicate shard or a disagreeing n is a failure naming it); (3) every other non-empty line is a suite path; (4) the multiset of suite paths over all files equals `tests/*.test.sh` of the tree it runs in, each exactly once. On failure it prints, one per line, every applicable message from this list (the list is complete; no other failure text): `ci: coverage: no assignment files in <dir>` (rule 1), `ci: coverage: bad header: <file>` (syntax only: a first line not matching `^# shard [1-9][0-9]*/[1-9][0-9]*$`), `ci: coverage: shard out of range: <file>` (a well-formed header with i greater than n; this case prints only this message for the header, never `bad header`), `ci: coverage: duplicate shard <i>: <file>` (a second file with the same i, named by the later file in sorted order), `ci: coverage: missing shard <i>`, `ci: coverage: shard count disagrees: <file>` (n differs from the first file's n in sorted order), `ci: coverage: suite in no shard: <path>`, `ci: coverage: suite in <k> shards: <path>` and `ci: coverage: unknown suite: <path>` (a listed path not in tests/*.test.sh), then exits 1; on success it prints `ci: coverage: <K> suites, each in exactly one of <n> shards`. Exit 64 for a usage error (no dir, dir missing). A file with a bad header or an out-of-range shard is excluded entirely: its suite lines are not counted, its i takes no shard slot and its n is not compared, so the remaining checks (missing shard, suite in no shard, suite in k shards) are computed over the other files only and print whatever they then find.

Wire the check into the workflow. Each bash shard step sets FM_CI_ASSIGNED_OUT=/tmp/suite-assigned/suite-assigned-${{ matrix.shard }}.txt, and a new step 'upload suite assignment' with `if: always()` uploads it as artifact `suite-assigned-${{ matrix.shard }}` (`if-no-files-found: ignore`; a missing file then fails the coverage check as a missing shard). The final `ci` job (ci.yml:256) gains, before 'every stage passed': (a) `actions/checkout@v4` with `sparse-checkout` listing `bin` and `tests` and no `ref:` override, so it checks out the same default ref the bash shards ran on (on a pull_request event the merge ref, on a push the pushed commit), which makes the suite list that of the run's own tree and lets a PR that adds or renames a suite pass; (b) `actions/download-artifact@v4` with `pattern: suite-assigned-*`, `merge-multiple: true`, `path: /tmp/suite-assigned`, `continue-on-error: true`; (c) a step 'every suite ran once' running `mkdir -p /tmp/suite-assigned && bash bin/ci.sh --coverage /tmp/suite-assigned`. The coverage step runs on push to main as well as on pull requests (no event condition), and its failure fails the `ci` job. The existing 'every stage passed' logic is unchanged. The header comment of ci.yml (:1-11) gets one sentence saying the ci job also checks every suite ran exactly once.

Tests, in tests/ci-sharding.test.sh (319 lines now; stay under 1200) using its existing `fixture` helper and FM_ROOT runs:
- With one timings file shared by all, run `--stage bash --shard i/3` for i=1..3 on a fixture with at least 7 trivially passing suites, each with FM_CI_ASSIGNED_OUT into one dir; `--coverage <dir>` exits 0 and reports 7 suites in 3 shards. Each file's first line is `# shard i/3`.
- Mixed timings: build two timings files A and B that put the fixture's suites into different 3-way partitions; first assert the precondition that the shard-1 assignment under A differs from shard-1 under B (so the test cannot pass vacuously). Run shard 1 with A and shards 2-3 with B; `--coverage` exits 1 and prints at least one `suite in no shard` or `suite in 2 shards` line naming a real fixture suite.
- Remove shard 2's file: exit 1 with `missing shard 2`. An empty dir: exit 1 with `no assignment files in <dir>`. Two files both headed `# shard 3/3` listing no suites (shard 1 and 2 files present and complete): exit 1 with `duplicate shard 3`. A file whose first line is `shard 2/3` (no `#`) or `# shard x/3`: exit 1 with `bad header: <file>`. A file headed `# shard 4/3`: exit 1 with `shard out of range: <file>` and no `bad header` line. A bad-header file that lists a suite also listed in a good file: that suite is not reported as in 2 shards (the bad file is excluded). A file whose header says `/4`: `shard count disagrees`. A file listing `tests/gone.test.sh`: `unknown suite`. A suite added to the fixture after the assignment files were written: `suite in no shard: <it>`.
- FM_CI_ASSIGNED_OUT unset: a shard run writes no assignment file anywhere under FM_ROOT or the test's temp dir. With no --shard, the file has header `# shard 1/1` and lists every suite.
- `--coverage` with `--stage bash`, with `--plan`, with no value, or with FM_ROOT='' exits 64.
Workflow pins in tests/ci-workflow.test.sh (extend its existing per-job block extraction, :24-36): a `bash-timings` job exists with no `if:` line and its step names `suite-timings-*`; the `bash` job block contains `needs: [bash-timings]`, `needs.bash-timings.outputs.timings`, `FM_CI_ASSIGNED_OUT` and `suite-assigned-${{ matrix.shard }}`, and does not contain `gh run download` (the single read); the `ci` job block contains `sparse-checkout`, `tests`, `pattern: suite-assigned-*` and `bin/ci.sh --coverage`, and the coverage step has no `github.event_name` condition; the `ci` job's checkout step has no `ref:` key (a `ref:` such as the fail-first jobs' `${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}`, ci.yml:187-188, would compare the merge ref's assignments against the head tree's suite list and fail falsely whenever main added or renamed a suite). A mutation check in the same style as tests/failfirst.test.sh:464-483: a copy of ci.yml with `gh run download` re-added to the bash job block makes the single-read pin fail, and a second copy with `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` added under the `ci` job's checkout `with:` makes the no-`ref:` pin fail.
Callers to keep green, checked by grep: tests/failfirst.test.sh (wvalue pins on fail-first-* and `ci needs`, :425-460), tests/ci-feature-suites.test.sh:45-47 (two `shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]` matrices), tests/ci-budget.test.sh:169-180 (FM_CI_MAX_SECONDS, timeout-minutes, bin/ci.sh, bun install, playwright pins), tests/ci-workflow.test.sh's existing assertions (every bun-installing job caches first: the `ci` job installs nothing), and tests/option-loop.test.sh (ci.sh stays exempt; the new flag uses the inline guard). bin/fm-failfirst.sh uses `--plan` only and is unaffected.

Docs, edited in place in their home sections (T-189 rule; nothing appended at the end of design.md):
- design/design.md §10 'CI' (starts about :2368), the paragraph beginning 'The bash stage records what each suite actually took' (about :2566-2590): the bash matrix no longer downloads timings per shard; one `bash-timings` job reads them once and hands the same text to all six shards; each shard writes its assignment (FM_CI_ASSIGNED_OUT) and uploads `suite-assigned-<shard>`; the `ci` job checks out bin/ and tests/ of the run's own ref and runs `bin/ci.sh --coverage`, failing unless every tests/*.test.sh ran in exactly one shard, on pull requests and on pushes to main; and the tests sentence lists the new coverage tests. Cite this task's incident (run 37218411231: 36 suites in no shard).
- design/design.md §7, the paragraph '**Fail-first is sharded like the bash suites (T-158).**' step 1 (about :1511-1515): 'the way each bash shard does' becomes 'the way the `bash timings` job does for the bash shards'.
- bin/ci.sh header comment (:1-25): FM_CI_ASSIGNED_OUT and `--coverage <dir>`.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml comments at :148-151 and :159 that call the fail-first read 'the bash shards' own': say the bash shards now read theirs once too, in `bash-timings`.

In flight and migration. No PR is open on this repository's main besides #159 (T-055, unrelated, not touching ci.yml). Once this lands, the 36 suites that a racing run could skip run on every PR; some may already be red on main because nothing guaranteed they ran. Firstmate runs, in parallel with this task, an unsharded audit of the bash stage on main in ubuntu:24.04 (FM_ROOT unset, FM_CI_MAX_SECONDS raised); any suite it finds red on main is handled by a separate scope-widening card or task, not by this spec, and this spec's worker does not fix unrelated suites. That audit also covers T-190 to T-195, which merged on possibly partial CI. Tasks dispatched after this one (cursor credential store, host record, worker notes) merge only after this task and are branch-updated onto it so their CI covers every suite.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates; on this PR's own CI the new `ci` job must show the coverage line `<K> suites, each in exactly one of 6 shards` with K equal to the number of tests/*.test.sh on the merge ref. Fail-first is expected from tests/ci-sharding.test.sh (the coverage, assignment and usage tests are red on base, where `--coverage` and FM_CI_ASSIGNED_OUT do not exist) and tests/ci-workflow.test.sh (the bash-timings, assignment and coverage pins are red on base). No vendor stub is involved: the fixtures are plain bash suites and the workflow is read as text.

Scope widening (2026-10-05): the --coverage program lives in bin/lib/fm_ci_checks.py as a `coverage` subcommand registered in its dispatch dict beside compile, variable-boundary, private-fetch and design-layout; bin/ci.sh calls it as `python3 "$_fm_code_dir/lib/fm_ci_checks.py" coverage <dir> <root>` like its other fm_ci_checks calls, with no embedded Python heredoc, so tests/config-python-extraction.test.sh stays green. Exit codes and message text are unchanged, so tests/ci-sharding.test.sh keeps passing unchanged.
